events.title: Lothair demands oaths
events.source: Three voices: Lothair's envoy is smooth and menacing; Warin's messenger is firm; Aldric is worried.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Lothair has come over the Alps and claims everything, the whole empire, as if his father's division at Worms had never been made. His men are riding from county to county demanding oaths. And there's one waiting in the hall now, asking for you.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The emperor Lothair greets the lord of Fontenay. He is the eldest son and the anointed emperor, and he asks only what is his due: your oath. Swear, and you keep your villa and everything you hold, confirmed by his hand. Refuse, and you will have chosen to stand against your emperor. He will remember that when the boy Charles has gone back to his mother.

script.speaker: steward
script.frame: Warin's messenger, arriving the same week
script.text: Count Warin stands with King Charles, as the late emperor commanded. He asks his men to swear nothing to Lothair's envoys, and to be ready to ride in the spring.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Lothair's armies are moving west toward Charles, my lord. Whatever happens between them, we'll hear of it by winter.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: And a third voice, my lord, quieter than the other two. Young Pippin's people have been to the gate again. With the old king and the old emperor both dead, they say your bonds have lapsed, and they ask which way a man of Pippin's would turn now: to the son, or to Count Warin and King Charles. Either answer is honest. Only one of them is safe.

knows: Lothair holds the crown and sword their father sent him; he claims that makes him emperor over all.
Charles holds the west under the Worms division of 839; Warin and Judith support him.
Louis the German has been pushed back to Bavaria by Lothair.
Pippin II is still fighting Charles in Aquitaine, and Lothair has asked Charles to go easy on him: a sign they are drawing together.
doesntKnow: That the truce will collapse, and that the brothers' armies will meet at Fontenoy in June.

events.title: The truce of Orléans

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Lothair and King Charles met near Orléans in November, with their armies close enough to see each other's fires. They didn't fight. They made a truce instead: Charles keeps Aquitaine, Septimania, Provence and ten counties between the Loire and the Seine, and they're to meet again at Attigny on the eighth of May to settle the rest. The truce says nothing plain about Burgundy, mind you, and that's the kind of thing men go to war over. Count Warin says to keep our horses fed through the winter.

knows: The truce terms and the May meeting at Attigny.
Lothair is courting Pippin II; Louis the German is gathering strength in the east.
doesntKnow: That the truce will break down and the meeting at Attigny will not settle anything.

hooks.trigger: The lord says he will set aside the army fine, meaning to sit the war out.

events.title: Warin's summons

script.speaker: steward
script.frame: with Count Warin's messenger, who reads
script.text: Count Warin to his men, greeting. The truce with Lothair is a dead letter; he has sent his men into King Charles's lands and courts the king's enemies in Aquitaine. King Charles calls his faithful men to him, and so do I. Muster at Autun before the end of April, armed and provisioned for three months, to march with the count.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: This is the one, my lord. Lothair, Charles, and Louis of Bavaria too, they say, all moving at once. If it comes to a battle, it'll be the biggest any of us has seen.

knows: The army fine for a free man who ignores the call-up is sixty solidi, seven hundred and twenty denarii.
Both armies will cross the region; staying home is not staying safe.

events.title: Bernard's camp

away.reason: in Duke Bernard's camp a few miles from Fontenoy

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, we can hear it from here. The armies are fighting at Fontenoy, a few miles off, and Duke Bernard sits in this camp with every man he brought and does not move. He is waiting to see who wins. His captains are divided; some want to ride for King Charles now, while it would count for something. If anyone can turn him, it is a man he trusts, and he trusts few enough.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the armies are near Auxerre, all of them, and their foraging parties range a long way out. Carts have been seen on the Avallon road, with armed men walking beside them and no banner anyone recognizes. If they come this way they will want grain and horses, and they will not ask twice.

events.title: After Fontenoy

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, it's done, and God help us, what a day it was. King Charles and King Louis beat Lothair near Fontenoy, south of Auxerre. Lothair had them hard pressed until Count Warin came up with the southern army and broke his line. Lothair has fled north. But the dead, my lord. They say no one living has seen so many killed in one day, Franks killing Franks. Duke Bernard sat it out a few miles off, waiting to see who'd win, and he's sent his son William to King Charles to make his peace.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: The bishops have ordered three days of fasting, for the dead of both sides. Brother against brother, my lord. I pray we never see the like again.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The men who came up with Count Warin's column are spoken of with pride in Autun, my lord, and you were among them. It will be remembered.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: We were on the wrong side of that field, my lord, and everyone in the county knows it. Count Warin has not sent for you yet. He will.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: There are houses in this valley with no man coming home: widows, heirs not yet grown, manses that will stand empty. Hard as it is to say, my lord, there are openings in that, for a marriage, for land, for a patron's hand.

variants.text: My lord, it's done, and God help us, what a day it was. King Charles and King Louis beat Lothair near Fontenoy, south of Auxerre. Lothair had them hard pressed until Count Warin came up with the southern army and broke his line. Lothair has fled north. But the dead, my lord. They say no one living has seen so many killed in one day, Franks killing Franks. And Duke Bernard came in for Charles at the end, with his own men, when it counted; they say it was you who turned him. The king will not forget either of you.

knows: The victory, Warin's decisive arrival, Lothair's flight.
The scale of the losses; the bishops' fast.
Bernard's absence from the battle, and his son William sent to Charles's court as a pledge.
doesntKnow: That Charles and Louis will swear a formal alliance at Strasbourg in February.

events.title: The comet and the oaths of Strasbourg

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: My lord, you'll have seen the comet this winter, night after night. The king's own men watched it closely, they say. After Fontenoy, I don't know whether to read it as a warning or a judgment.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: King Charles and King Louis met at Strasbourg in February and swore an alliance before both their armies: each king in the other's tongue, so every man could understand, and then the soldiers swore too. They mean to finish Lothair together.

hooks.trigger: The lord explains the comet as a natural thing, calmly and as a matter of learning.
The lord mocks the fear of the comet.
The lord remarks that the Strasbourg oath, sworn in the soldiers' tongue, is a rare thing written down in the common speech.

events.title: Lothair abandons Aachen; peace talks near Mâcon

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Lothair is finished in the north. Charles and Louis marched on Aachen in March; Lothair's men were meant to hold the Moselle crossings, and they scattered when the armies came up. He's fled south toward the Rhône without a fight, and the bishops at Aachen have declared him unfit to rule. Now he's asking for peace, and here's the strange part: the three brothers are to meet this very season on an island in the Saône, near Mâcon. Barely a day's ride from here.

knows: The kings' camps will need grain and horses; in a hungry year that trade is very profitable, and very visible.
Charles is taking Toulouse from Bernard this year.

hooks.trigger: The lord sells grain or horses to the kings' camps at the talks.

effects.record: The lord supplied the kings' camps at the Saône talks.

hooks.trigger: The lord offers hospitality to envoys travelling to the talks.

events.title: A truce, a poor harvest, and a royal wedding

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the kings' men have been meeting all autumn to divide the empire, and they still can't agree, so the truce is extended. Truth is, nobody can afford a war this year: the harvest has been poor everywhere, and all three kings know it. And King Charles is to be married this month, to the lady Ermentrude, a niece of Count Adalard the seneschal. Not our late count, my lord, a different Adalard.

events.title: The war for Toulouse
events.source: Warin's household calls Bernard a traitor; Bernard's people call Charles ungrateful.

script.speaker: steward
script.frame: with Count Warin's messenger, who reads
script.text: Count Warin to his men. Bernard, once duke, has refused the king's judgment on Toulouse, joined himself to Pippin the rebel, and driven the king's count out of the city by force. King Charles sends the count south against him. Every man who holds of the count is to muster at Autun armed and provisioned for the campaign in Gothia.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: And there was another rider before the count's, my lord, one of Lord Bernard's, who would not come into the hall. The duke asks the men who kept faith with him before to come south and stand with him now. He calls the king ungrateful; the count calls him a traitor. You cannot ride with both.

knows: In 842 Charles took Toulouse from Bernard and gave it to another count; Bernard would not accept it.
Pippin II holds much of Aquitaine and Bernard has allied with him.
doesntKnow: That Bernard will end in Charles's hands.
That the siege of Toulouse next spring will fail.

events.title: The Treaty of Verdun

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, it's settled, at Verdun. The empire is cut in three. Louis takes the east, Charles the west, and Lothair keeps the title of emperor and a long middle kingdom from Frisia down through Lyon and Provence to Italy. We're King Charles's, for good. But mark this: the far bank of the Saône, and Lyon with it, belongs to Lothair now. We live on a border, my lord.

knows: Trade across the Saône is now trade with another kingdom; Lothair's men are a river away.
Good grounds for building defenses and for border diplomacy.

hooks.trigger: The lord sets a watch on the Saône crossings or begins to strengthen the villa's defenses against the border.

events.record: At Verdun the empire was cut in three; the Saône became a border.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, King Charles held an assembly at Coulaines, near Le Mans, and made a pact with his bishops and great men. He promised to rule with their counsel, and not to take a man's lands or offices from him without just cause and a fair judgment. That's worth more to us than you might think, my lord: a benefice is safer under a king who has sworn that.

hooks.trigger: The lord has the villa's title and the count's confirmation written up and witnessed under the king's new promise.

battle.historical: Pippin II's garrison holds Toulouse; Charles's siege fails.
cards: scaling ladders and sorties at Toulouse
battle.interimLine: The siege of Toulouse, with you before the walls or behind them, is not yet written in this chronicle, my lord. The city held, as it happens, and you came home.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Lord Bernard's luck has run out. He is to be brought before King Charles this spring, by safe-conduct they say, and nobody who knows the king believes the safe-conduct will hold. Count Warin wants him dead; the king wants Toulouse out of that family for good. If anything is to be done for him, it must be done in these weeks, and it will cost whoever does it.

outcomes.canChange: Bernard is not a keystone. A man of Bernard's who warns him not to trust the safe-conduct, escorts him to Septimania, or beats the force sent to seize him may save him (high risk; the lord becomes Charles's enemy). A man of Warin's present at the capture may let him slip away (enemy_warin if discovered). A man with high renown may intercede with Charles for mercy (moderate chance; costs royal favor). If none of that is done, or it fails, Bernard is executed in May.

events.title: Bernard is dead
events.source: Warin's household is satisfied; Bernard's old followers are grieving and afraid.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Bernard is dead. Duke Bernard, who gave you Fontenay. He was brought before King Charles in the spring, and the king had him put to death as a traitor. Whatever you think of him, my lord, and he was never short of enemies, he was the man who took a chance on you. His sons are alive: the elder, William, is at the king's court, and the little one is still with his mother. They say the king means to keep Toulouse out of that family for good.

She has the younger boy with her and nothing else that is safe; William is a hostage in all but name. She asks for nothing in words. She asks for a great deal between them.

events.title: Bernard lives

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Lord Bernard is alive and in Septimania, under Pippin's protection, and everybody between here and Toulouse knows whose doing that was. He has lost Toulouse and he will not get it back; he is near fifty and sidelined. But he lives, and his sons have a father. Count Warin's people are saying your name in a certain tone of voice. So, I am told, is the king's household.

events.record: Bernard lived, sidelined in Septimania, with the lord's name on it.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, terrible news from Aquitaine. While King Charles sat before Toulouse, he sent for reinforcements from the north. Pippin's men caught them on the march in the Angoumois and cut them to pieces. Abbot Hugh, the king's own uncle, is dead, and others with him; great lords taken for ransom. The king has given up the siege. Pippin is stronger than ever.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Your side is winning in the south, my lord, for now. They are saying the king will have to recognise Pippin in Aquitaine before long.
